inventory_summary: National parks, hunting zones and MPAs are PA categories under the wildlife regime (Décret 2011-394); Pendjari NP is under delegated management (6NR). The NBSAP Tableau 1 (DGFRN 2013) gives official counts by category (2 national parks, 4 zones cynégétiques, 46 forêts classées, 6 périmètres de reboisement) but no names; two MPAs were created in 2022. cenagref.net was not used (reported hijacked). Comparison: the sources reviewed list 9 nationally designated or proposed areas; 3 are catalogued here, and 6 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 4 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

The legal inventory is the annex 'Rede Nacional Inicial de Áreas Protegidas' of Decreto-Lei n.º 3/2003 of 24 February 2003 (regime jurídico dos espaços naturais; amended by Decreto-Lei n.º 44/2006), which declares 47 areas by island in six categories (Parque Nacional, Parque Natural, Reserva Natural, Monumento Natural, Paisagem Protegida, Sítio de Interesse Científico). Individual areas are subsequently delimited by Decreto-Regulamentar and given management plans by Resolução; some categories and limits have changed since 2003 (e.g. Barreiro e Figueira now a Paisagem Protegida). All 47 annex entries are recorded below with the 2003 category; later instruments verified in FAOLEX are added to legalStatus. Later additions to the network (if any) were not systematically searched. The 2003 annex is an official list but only as a scanned gazette page (not machine-readable). Comparison: the sources reviewed list 47 nationally designated or proposed areas; 20 are catalogued here (1 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 27 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 4 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

Parks and reserves are managed by the Office Ivoirien des Parcs et Réserves (OIPR) under Loi n° 2002-102, whose Annexes 1-2 are the official list as of 2002 (8 national parks, 6 reserves with creating instrument and area). Later creations are by decree (2013-2026), traced via FAOLEX/LEAP, the national CBD CHM and Council-of-Ministers communiqués. Forêts classées (~231-234, SODEFOR) were not enumerated. oipr.ci was not used. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 26 nationally designated or proposed areas; 17 are catalogued here (1 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 9 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 6 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

Wildlife protected areas are designated under the Biodiversity/Wildlife Act 2003 and managed by the Department of Parks and Wildlife Management (DPWM); forest reserves/parks are under the Department of Forestry. The best official list found is Table 1 'Protected Areas of the Gambia' in the revised NBSAP (March 2015), giving 22 entries (7 established parks/reserves, 1 proposed national park, 1 community wildlife reserve and 13 community conservation areas then 'in process'). The 6th national report (2019) repeats the count of 22 wildlife protected areas (8 reserves/national parks + 14 community-based conservation areas) without names. No DPWM-published list was used (dpwm.gov.gm reported hijacked/dead). Comparison: the sources reviewed list 24 nationally designated or proposed areas; 7 are catalogued here (2 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 17 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 3 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

Wildlife protected areas are managed by the Wildlife Division of the Forestry Commission and are legally established by the Wildlife Reserves Regulations 1971 (L.I. 710) and its amendments (kept in force by the Wildlife Resources Management Act 2023, Act 1115). The NBSAP (Nov 2016, Table 4, source FDMP 2016) gives the most complete official list with areas and years. Forest reserves (~280) are managed by the Forest Services Division and were not enumerated. The Forestry Commission website was not used (reported hijacked/dead). Comparison: the sources reviewed list 18 nationally designated or proposed areas; 14 are catalogued here (1 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 4 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 6 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

No published official list of Guinea's protected areas was found. Guinea's PoWPA document (CBD) says the national protected-area network was 'validated' in 2010 with 53 identified protected areas, many without validated creation acts, but gives no list. Management lies with the Office Guinéen des Parcs Nationaux et Réserves de Faune (OGPNRF) and the forestry administration; Mount Nimba is managed by CEGENS. The most detailed descriptive source is the 2008 IUCN/PAPACO management-effectiveness evaluation of 12 areas (hosted on Guinea's national CBD clearing-house), which itself warns that the legal status of most areas has not been updated since independence. Records below combine that evaluation with Guinea's 6th (2018) and 7th (2026) CBD reports and the Haut Niger creation decree; legal status is uncertain for several sites. Ramsar sites are handled separately. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 14 nationally designated or proposed areas; 9 are catalogued here (3 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 5 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 15 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

The Sistema Nacional de Áreas Protegidas (SNAP) is managed by the Instituto da Biodiversidade e das Áreas Protegidas (IBAP) under the Lei-Quadro das Áreas Protegidas (Decreto-Lei 5-A/2011, replacing Decreto-Lei 3/97). IBAP's website lists the protected areas and publishes the creation decrees (scanned Boletim Oficial pages), which were checked for the 2000, 2005, 2011 and 2017 decrees. The 6th CBD report (2019) states the SNAP covers 26.3% of the territory (~750,000 ha) with 8 protected areas plus 3 ecological corridors created by Decrees 11–15/2017. The list appears complete for state protected areas; community forests (104) are not enumerated. Note: the IBAP website (ibapgbissau.org) also carries unrelated spam blog posts, suggesting partial compromise; facts were cross-checked against the decree scans and NR6. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 11 nationally designated or proposed areas; 6 are catalogued here (5 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 5 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 4 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

inventory_summary: The Forestry Development Authority (FDA) is the statutory PA authority (National Forestry Reform Law 2006; Protected Forest Areas Network Act 2003). Its June 2026 Kwa gazettement package states the network comprises five legally established PAs and lists the proposed PAs; the NBSAP 2017-2025 (Table 10, source FDA) gives areas. No machine-readable list found. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 16 nationally designated or proposed areas; 6 are catalogued here (2 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 10 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 5 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

No standalone official register was found. The most explicit official statement is Mauritania's 6th CBD national report (2019, section 7.2 'Situation des aires protégées'), which lists two national parks (Banc d'Arguin, Diawling), a recently created third park (Awleigatt), the Cap Blanc satellite reserve and the (unclassified) Chat Tboul reserve, plus several areas under study. The two main parks are public administrative establishments with their own laws/decrees and official websites (pnba.mr, pnd.mr); a Direction des aires protégées et du littoral (DAPL) exists within the environment ministry. The 'Zones protégées' page of the national CBD clearing-house (mr.chm-cbd.net) reproduces outdated WCMC-derived entries and was not used. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 7 nationally designated or proposed areas; 4 are catalogued here (3 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 3 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 4 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

Federal national parks are managed by the Nigeria National Park Service (NPS) under the National Park Service Act (Cap N65 LFN 2004, amended 2006), whose s.50 lists the seven pre-existing parks. Ten additional parks were declared by the National Park (Declaration) Order 2022 (National Assembly concurrence March 2023; NPS says gazetted) and are being handed over by the states in batches (Hadejia Wetlands, Oba Hills and Marhai in 2024; Kampe in Feb 2025), giving 17 national parks per NPS. Game reserves and forest reserves are state-managed; no official machine-readable or enumerable national list of them was found. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 18 nationally designated or proposed areas; 11 are catalogued here, and 7 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 16 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

No single consolidated, current official list was found online. Protected areas are split between the Direction des Parcs Nationaux (DPN: national parks, special/fauna reserves), the Direction des Aires Marines Communautaires Protégées (DAMCP, created by decree 2012-543: marine protected areas and coastal community reserves) and the forestry service DEFCCS (213 forêts classées, sylvopastoral reserves, hunting zones). The best official lists found are: the DPN's PoWPA document (table of 16 DPN-administered areas, c. 2011), the 2013 National MPA Strategy (14 coastal areas), Senegal's 2018 AEWA national-report annex (22 sites incl. later AMPs), and individual creation decrees (2004, 2014, 2020, 2023). Lists are dated and partial; the DPN and DAMCP websites were not used (reported hijacked/dead). Comparison: the sources reviewed list 28 nationally designated or proposed areas; 19 are catalogued here (9 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 9 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 9 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

The National Protected Area Authority (NPAA), created by the National Protected Areas Authority and Conservation Trust Fund Act 2012, manages national parks and wildlife sanctuaries; forest reserves remain with the Forestry Division, and the four estuarine Marine Protected Areas were declared by the Ministry of Fisheries and Marine Resources. NPAA's website has a 'List of National Protected Areas' page, but it was empty when fetched (Oct 2026) and the site contains template placeholder content. The best official descriptions are the NBSAP 2017–2026 (protected-area categories under the Wildlife Conservation Act 1972, gazetted national parks, Table 9 of major forest-estate components, Table 2 of estuarine MPAs) and the 6th CBD national report (2020). No complete official register was found. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 22 nationally designated or proposed areas; 10 are catalogued here (2 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 12 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 1 Ramsar site for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

The Ministère de l'Environnement et des Ressources Forestières (MERF) is responsible for PAs. Of 83 legally classified PAs (to 1990), a requalification programme (since 1999; décret 2003-237/PR) retained 10-14 priority PAs covering ~578,000 ha. No consolidated official list with legal acts exists in sources seen; records combine the government PoWPA table, NBSAP 2014, 6NR (2018) and the UICN 2008 RAPPAM. A new law on creation and management of PAs was adopted by the National Assembly in August 2026 (promulgation not verified). Comparison: the sources reviewed list 14 nationally designated or proposed areas; 6 are catalogued here (1 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 8 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 4 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

The national conservation-area network is managed by INBAC (Instituto Nacional da Biodiversidade e Áreas de Conservação, under the ministry responsible for the environment, currently the Ministério da Cultura, Turismo e Ambiente per INBAC park pages). INBAC's website lists 14 areas — 9 national parks, 1 regional natural park (Chimalavera) and 4 reserves — with creating instruments and areas on each page; this matches the counts in the 2019-2025 NBSAP and INBAC's November 2023 status report (156,909.9 km2, 12.58% of the territory). No machine-readable register exists. The legal framework is Lei 8/20 (Áreas de Conservação Ambiental), amended by Lei 12/21. Four further areas, including the first marine conservation area (Baía dos Tigres), are being created but no creating instrument was found. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 18 nationally designated or proposed areas; 10 are catalogued here, and 8 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 1 Ramsar site for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

inventory_summary: No public protected-area register from the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (DWNP) was found online (DWNP has no standalone website; the Botswana Tourism site returned errors). The authoritative list is statutory: the Wildlife Conservation and National Parks Act (Cap. 38:01) declares national parks (First Schedule), game reserves and sanctuaries (Second Schedule), wildlife management areas (Third Schedule) and controlled hunting areas (Fourth Schedule). The freely available consolidated text (FAOLEX) runs to 2007; the Sua Pan Flamingo Sanctuary (S.I. 38 of 2010) was added from its own order. Forest reserves come from the Forest (Declaration of Forest Reserves) Order. The current (2023-2024 amended) consolidated Act is behind a paywall, so later changes may be missing. Category totals from the 5th CBD report (2015, Table 5): national parks 44,390 km2 (7%); game reserves 59,590 + 408 km2 (10%); legislated WMAs 72,090 km2 (23%) plus 65,780 km2 not legislated; forest reserves 4,095.4 km2 (1%). DWNP's PoWPA submission: 'About 40% of the Botswana’s land area has been devoted to protected areas, with 17% being national parks and game reserves'. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 29 nationally designated or proposed areas; 10 are catalogued here, and 19 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 1 Ramsar site for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

The Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA, Nature Conservation Sector) maintains the official list of natural protectorates declared by Prime Ministerial decree under Law No. 102 of 1983. Its July 2026 list (English and Arabic PDFs) enumerates all 31 protectorates with declaration year, area, governorate, management type and declaring/amending decrees; this matches the count of 31 (up to 2025) stated on the EEAA protectorates page. The list appears complete for nationally declared protectorates. It is a PDF table, not a dataset, and gives no coordinates or boundaries. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 31 nationally designated or proposed areas; 20 are catalogued here (3 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 11 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 4 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

No consolidated official list was retrievable online: the ANPN (Agence Nationale des Parcs Nationaux) website did not resolve/respond. The inventory here is assembled from the founding legal texts: the 13 decrees of 30 August 2002 classifying the national parks (FAOLEX/LEAP; governed since by Loi 003/2007) and Décret 00161/PR of 31 May 2017, which creates 9 marine parks and 11 aquatic reserves with areas and boundaries. Counts are confirmed by Gabon's 6th national report to the CBD (2019). Other protected areas (presidential reserve, arboreta, hunting domains, proposed sites) come from the 2012 PoWPA action plan and the 2019 national report and are dated or partly verified. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 46 nationally designated or proposed areas; 18 are catalogued here (5 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 28 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 8 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

ANAC (Administração Nacional das Áreas de Conservação) administers the national system of conservation areas and its website lists 10 national parks, 2 national reserves and 1 special reserve (plus transfrontier areas), but its 'sobre' text is out of date ('7 Parques e 7 Reservas Nacionais') and it does not list environmental protection areas, partial reserves or municipal parks. Creation instruments are decrees published in the Boletim da República (several available on FAOLEX). Hunting areas (20 coutadas oficiais, 9 blocos de caça, 13 community programmes, 31 fazendas do bravio) are stated by ANAC without a published list. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 16 nationally designated or proposed areas; 11 are catalogued here, and 5 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 2 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

State protected areas are managed by the Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism (MEFT); its website lists 20 state protected areas (national parks, game parks, recreation resorts, Cape Cross Seal Reserve, South West Nature Reserve) with size and proclamation year per park, but no machine-readable register and no Government Notice references. Communal conservancies are registered by MEFT under s.24A of the Nature Conservation Ordinance; the most complete public list is NACSO's table (86 conservancies, matching MEFT's stated 86) plus NACSO's compilation of gazette numbers. A further conservancy (Ekango Lyomongwa) was gazetted in September 2025. Community forests (Forest Act 2001) and inland fisheries reserves (Inland Fisheries Resources Act 2003) were enumerated directly from the Government Gazettes hosted by NACSO. The marine protected area is the Namibian Islands' Marine Protected Area (Marine Resources Act 2000). Comparison: the sources reviewed list 166 nationally designated or proposed areas; 15 are catalogued here, and 151 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 5 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

No consolidated official list or protected-area authority website was found. The inventory is reconstructed from the founding legal texts in the Diário da República (via FAOLEX): Laws 6/2006 and 7/2006 creating the two terrestrial natural parks, and Decree-Laws 02/2026 (national MPA network framework) and 03/2026 (first two MPAs of São Tomé). The six MPAs planned around Príncipe are to be classified by a separate Príncipe regional instrument, which was not found. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 4 nationally designated or proposed areas; 2 are catalogued here, and 2 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 1 Ramsar site for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

No single consolidated official list. Inventories are split by managing authority: TANAPA (national parks; 21 park sections on its website, Kigosi National Park was revoked by GN 616 of 2023), TAWA (an official table of game reserves, game controlled areas and wildlife management areas with area, region and gazettement GN), NCAA (Ngorongoro Conservation Area), the Marine Parks and Reserves Unit (3 marine parks + 15 marine reserves, Tanzania mainland), and TFS (465 forest reserves incl. 25 nature forest reserves and 18 bee reserves; no public list). Zanzibar's protected areas are managed separately by the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar; no official Zanzibar list could be fetched. Legal instruments (GNs) are indexed on TanzLII. The TAWA table is the most complete official list; the TANAPA list comes from the site's park sections, not from a stated list. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 124 nationally designated or proposed areas; 31 are catalogued here, and 93 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 4 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

inventory_summary: Uganda Wildlife Authority manages the wildlife conservation areas and states their counts (10 national parks, 12 wildlife reserves, 5 community wildlife management areas, 13 wildlife sanctuaries) but its website names only the national parks and 11 wildlife reserves. The legal declarations are statutory instruments under the Uganda Wildlife Act (most from 2003, SI 41–64 of 2003), indexed on ULII. The National Forestry Authority manages 506 central forest reserves (no list published on its website); local forest reserves are managed by district governments. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 31 nationally designated or proposed areas; 22 are catalogued here (1 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 9 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 12 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

Wildlife protected areas are designated and managed by the Ministère des Forêts et de la Faune (MINFOF) under forest and wildlife law n° 94/01 of 1994, replaced by law n° 2024/08 of 24 July 2024. The MINFOF website (minfof.cm) returned 403 Forbidden. MINFOF and WRI publish the official register as the open file geodatabase of the Interactive Forest Atlas of Cameroon (2025 edition) and as a 'Domaine forestier' poster dated December 2025. The geodatabase lists 37 wildlife PAs: 22 national parks, 4 wildlife reserves and 5 wildlife sanctuaries created, plus 3 proposed national parks and 3 proposed sanctuaries. It also lists 70 hunting zones (ZIC/ZICGC) and 59 forest reserves. Cameroon's 7th CBD national report (March 2026) counts 109 protected areas: 22 national parks, 5 wildlife reserves, 6 sanctuaries, 3 zoological gardens, 1 botanical garden, 45 ZIC and 27 ZICGC. That is one wildlife reserve and one sanctuary more than the MINFOF GIS; the sanctuary is probably Kilum-Ijim (created by a 2004 decree), and the extra reserve could not be identified. Creating or classifying acts were checked on FAOLEX for 13 areas. For the rest, the legal status rests on the MINFOF GIS record. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 45 nationally designated or proposed areas; 30 are catalogued here, and 15 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 7 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

No consolidated official list was retrievable online: the ACFAP (Agence congolaise de la faune et des aires protégées, created by Loi 34-2012) website did not respond. Congo's 6th national report to the CBD (MEFDD, September 2017) gives the most recent government table: 15 protected areas (4 national parks, 7 reserves, 2 sanctuaries, 2 hunting domains), 3,903,010 ha (11%). The OFAC/COMIFAC 'État des aires protégées 2015' gives the same 15 sites with creation texts. This file adds Ogooué-Lékéti National Park (Décret 2022-1921) and two community marine reserves adopted by the Council of Ministers in October 2023, whose report speaks of 17 parks and reserves. Most entries are checked against the creation decrees on FAOLEX; the Mont Fouari complex and Tsoulou rely on the CBD report and EdAP 2015. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 21 nationally designated or proposed areas; 13 are catalogued here (4 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 8 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 13 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.

inventory_summary: The Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature (ICCN) manages nearly all protected areas (Luki and Yangambi are exceptions). It publishes counts but no list: its website (2026) states 8 national parks, 63 hunting domains and reserves, 4 botanical and 4 zoological gardens. It names the 8 parks, the Okapi faunal reserve, Lomako-Yokokala, Tumba-Lediima, the Couloir Vert, and in a 2026 news item Bili-Uere, Itombwe and Abumonbazi. Older government reports give 7 national parks and 57 or 63 reserves and hunting domains, plus 3 biosphere reserves and 117 forest reserves (NR4 2009, ICCN strategy 2012, NBSAP 2016). The 6th national report (2019) has a list, but it is copied from WDPA and was not used. This inventory comes from creation and delimitation acts on FAOLEX (many from the Journal Officiel) and UNESCO pages. An IUCN/PACO 2010 assessment of 19 sites (labelled NGO) fills gaps. Most of the 57-63 hunting domains and reserves are not enumerated. Comparison: the sources reviewed list 40 nationally designated or proposed areas; 26 are catalogued here (2 as an extra designation on an already catalogued area), and 14 are verified but not yet mapped because no openly licensed location was found. The catalogue also holds 4 Ramsar sites for this country. Coverage has not been verified as exhaustive.
